hypotheses.text: Formal diagnostic criteria for autism spectrum disorder (HP:0000729) are met in only 24% (approximately 8 of 33) of individuals in the primary LRRC7 cohort, contradicting earlier binned estimates of 50% to 70% autistic behavior.
hypotheses.rationale: Prior binned approximations suggested autism or autistic features occur in 50-70% of LRRC7-related cases. However, primary cohort reporting from Willim et al. (2024) documents an exact ASD frequency of 24%, indicating that strict diagnostic ASD is far lower than broad behavioral impairment unless broader sub-diagnostic social-communication traits are lumped into the term.

evidence.text: Willim et al. report that several individuals were diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder at a prevalence of 24% across their multicenter cohort of 33 individuals.

hypotheses.text: The exact cohort frequency of seizures/epilepsy (HP:0001250) in LRRC7-related disorder is 18.2% (6 of 33 patients), demonstrating that LRRC7-related synaptopathy presents with a significantly lower seizure penetrance than classic postsynaptic density channelopathies like SYNGAP1.
hypotheses.rationale: Previous literature bins seizures between 20% and 40%, whereas SYNGAP1 encephalopathy shows >80% intractable seizures. Confirming whether the exact numerator is 6 out of 33 establishes an objective penetrance rate of under 20% for LRRC7.

evidence.text: Willim et al. report that varying types of seizures were observed in exactly six patients within their 33-individual cohort.

source.quote: Here, we investigated a proband presenting global developmental delay (GDD), tonic seizures, failure to thrive, mild microcephaly, intellectual disability (ID), and hypotonia.

hypotheses.text: Hyperphagia-associated obesity (HP:0001513) is restricted to an exact frequency of 15.2% (5 of 33 individuals) in the primary LRRC7 cohort, distinguishing a discrete neuroendocrine/metabolic subgroup rather than a universal syndromic hallmark.
hypotheses.rationale: Hyperphagia and obesity have been identified as a distinguishing metabolic finding compared to other synaptopathies, but vague descriptors ('several cases', '<35%') need replacement with the definitive numerator/denominator (5 of 33) to determine its predictive utility.

evidence.text: Willim et al. identify hyperphagia-associated obesity in several individuals, with snippet data indicating five patients exhibited moderate obesity.

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact denominator-adjusted frequencies of non-behavioral somatic findings (such as hypotonia HP:0001252, microcephaly HP:0000252, and gastrointestinal symptoms) across individual supplement tables of Willim et al. 2024 versus contiguous 1p31.1 microdeletion cases?
new_directions.rationale: Dissecting whether mild microcephaly and hypotonia are caused by LRRC7 haploinsufficiency directly or by adjacent 1p31.1 microdeletion genes (as reported in Mikhailova & Garg 2025) will clarify true gene-specific physical signs.

new_directions.question_text: Does the presence of incomplete penetrance in Willim et al. 2024 correlate strictly with transmitted familial missense variants versus de novo loss-of-function variants?
new_directions.rationale: OMIM entry #621415 cites Willim et al. 2024 for incomplete penetrance. Establishing the exact numerator and denominator of unaffected or mildly affected carriers according to variant type is essential for clinical counseling.
